papers.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
papers.abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].

papers.title: Geometric knowledge spaces, Attention pairing and Architectures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a geometric approach to deriving attention mechanisms and exploring potential new transformer architectures. We begin by formalizing the notions of knowledge worlds and attention pairings, then demonstrate how this framework naturally leads to the architectures of standard attention, causal attention, linear attention, tensor attention, and recurrent neural networks. Finally, we introduce several new geometric spaces that may inspire novel neural network architectures.

papers.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

papers.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
papers.abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.

papers.title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
papers.abstract: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together. This discriminant is a hypersurface, parametrized by the logarithmic Horn uniformization. Hurwitz forms of toric varieties yield a degree formula, and a description of leading coefficients. We emphasize applications and computations.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlev\'e equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlev\'e equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.

papers.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
papers.abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.

papers.title: Derived categories of threefolds near the Noether line
papers.abstract: We show that derived categories of canonical stacks associated to general threefolds in the principal component of the moduli space of canonical threefolds on the refined Noether line are semiorthogonally indecomposable. First we generalize a criterion of Kawatani-Okawa for the indecomposability of derived categories of surfaces of general type to higher-dimensional varieties and stacks. And then we generalize a construction of Kobayashi and Hu-Zhang and a classification result of Coughlan-Pignatelli to the second and third Noether lines to show that our criterion applies to these canonical stacks.

papers.title: Germwise singular Fourier--Mukai partnerships
papers.abstract: We study how local behavior on the base controls whether integral transforms induce fully faithful functors or equivalences between singularity categories of proper flat families. By working with \'{e}tale germs, we show (under mild hypotheses) that the loci where this happens are open and are compatible with \'{e}tale base change. Moreover, we give examples, exhibit an autoequivalence of the singularity category which detects regularity of the base, and compute these loci for arithmetic families.

papers.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
papers.abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.

papers.title: On the gap of thresholds
papers.abstract: We propose an algorithm to compute the gap numbers of log canonical thresholds, anticanonical thresholds, and $\mathbb{R}$-complementary thresholds for surface pairs with a given rational hyperstandard coefficient set. As an example, we compute these gap numbers for a special hyperstandard set that appears in the effective boundedness of $n$-complements for surface pairs.

papers.title: The recent counterexamples to the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman Ulrich problem (2003) and to Hochster's small Cohen-Macaulay conjecture (1973): a survey, with a generalization to arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: In September 2026 four preprints and an AI-generated manuscript moved one numerical obstruction from projective geometry to local algebra. For a smooth complex projective surface $Y$ with an ample, globally generated divisor $H$ such that $H^2<\sigma(Y)$, the signature, one obtains in turn: no Ulrich bundles when $H$ is very ample (Anghel, arXiv:2609.02718; extended to every dimension by Lopez, arXiv:2609.06678), answering negatively the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman question of 2003 for sheaves supported on the whole variety; no arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, i.e. section rings without graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules in characteristic zero (Anghel, arXiv:2609.15589); and complete local domains without small Cohen-Macaulay modules, counterexamples to Hochster's 1973 conjecture, if $K_Y\equiv4H$ (Chen, arXiv:2609.24142, proposed) or $\sigma>2H^2$ (OpenAI, released 6 October). We recall the definitions and main statements, and add two things. First, through a finite projection to $\mathbb P^2$ and an identity already present in the OpenAI manuscript, the three obstructions become one variance identity; for surfaces this explains the factor $2$ between the graded bound $\sigma\le H^2$ and the local $\sigma\le2H^2$. Second, we generalize the argument of the OpenAI manuscript to every dimension $m\ge2$, with complete proofs: if $X$ is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $m$ and $H$ an ample, globally generated divisor, a small Cohen-Macaulay module over the completed section ring of $(X,H)$ forces $(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{m-2}\le(m+4)H^m$. Consequently the completed section rings of all Hesse pairs, including the ball quotient of the first preprint, have no small Cohen-Macaulay module, and products of Hesse surfaces with projective spaces give complete local domains with an isolated singularity, of every dimension $\ge3$, without small Cohen-Macaulay modules.

papers.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
papers.abstract: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.

papers.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
papers.abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

papers.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors
papers.abstract: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $\Gamma_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.

papers.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

papers.title: Topological degree of fewnomial maps
papers.abstract: We study the topological degree on the positive orthant of a map $F:\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\mathcal{A}$ of $N=n+k+1$ monomials. This degree is well defined under a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope, which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. We give three formulas for it, all in terms of signs of maximal minors. The first one is a Viro formula: the degree is a signed count of the simplices of a regular triangulation of $\mathcal{A}$ which are positively decorated in the sense of Bihan, Santos and Spaenlehauer. The second one is a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and the third one a sum over the vertices of the polyhedron of the Gale dual system. As a consequence, the degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We also obtain a Descartes rule of signs for the degree and, in the generic case, the upper bound $|\deg F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the largest number of facets of a $d$-polytope with $N$ vertices. This bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsg{\aa}rd, we show that the set of possible degrees is symmetric in $n$ and $k$. Since a nonzero degree forces a positive zero, our formulas give sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity statements for their number.

papers.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
papers.abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.

papers.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.

papers.title: Exactness property of Breuil-Kisin functors and Bloch-Kato Selmer groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field and $T$ a lattice in a semistable representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ with Hodge-Tate weights in $[0, r]$. Assuming $0\leq r<p-1$, we prove that for a semistable extension of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by $T$, the corresponding sequence of strongly divisible modules is exact. Analogous statements are proved for Breuil-Kisin modules and for prismatic $F$-crystals for all $r\geq 0$. In the crystalline case, we deduce that the integral Bloch-Kato Selmer group $H^1_f(K, T)$ is computed by $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ in the category of crystalline strongly divisible modules. Using further exactness results, we define a tensor product of strongly divisible modules, which commutes with the functors to Galois representations. As an application, we show that for abelian varieties $A_1, A_2$ over $K$ with good reduction, the cup product map $\delta_1\cup\delta_2:A_1(K)\otimes A_2(K)\rightarrow H^2(K, T_p(A_1)\otimes T_p(A_2))$ induced by the Kummer sequences of $A_1, A_2$ factors through an $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ group of strongly divisible modules. In the appendix we generalize further the main exactness results to coherent reflexive $F$-gauges.

papers.title: Spherical Milnor Spaces II: Projective Quotients and Higher Topological Structures
papers.abstract: We study projective and semidirect quotients of the spherical Milnor construction and develop a step-by-step lifting obstruction from their explicit spherical local sections. The resulting transition functions produce a twisted Cech 2-cocycle for any specified compatible extension with abelian kernel. When the kernel is $U(1)$ and the sign acts by complex conjugation, taking logarithms yields a twisted Dixmier--Douady obstruction under stated sheaf hypotheses. We identify its projective-operator interpretation when an additional representation is supplied, without attempting a classification of K-theory twists. We also investigate descent of differential-geometric structures and, under restricted-operator hypotheses, Schwinger cocycles and lifting gerbes for loop groups.

papers.title: Rigidity of multisections to the universal cubic plane curve
papers.abstract: We study the following question of Farb: For which positive integers n is it possible to choose n distinct points continuously on every smooth cubic plane curve? This paper is a continuation of the work of Banerjee-Chen. We prove that such choice is unique up to homotopy for n=27 (smallest open case), and does not exist for n=36k+18.

papers.title: An Explicit Belyi Map for the Wiman Sextic and Cusp Forms for a Noncongruence Subgroup
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explicitly determine an algebraic Belyi function on a unique smooth projective model $\widetilde{W}$ of the Wiman sextic curve $W$ and describe its complex uniformization in terms of modular functions associated with a certain noncongruence subgroup $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}} \subset {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we give a direct proof of the unbounded denominators conjecture for weight $2$ cusp forms with respect to $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}}$. The conjecture is now known in full generality by the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang, following earlier progress including work of Dong, Lin, and Ng. Our proof, however, uses a degeneration of $\widetilde{W}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{5}$ together with explicit Puiseux series expansions and is substantially different from the methods employed in their work.

papers.title: Relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and $p$-adic differential equations
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an affinoid rigid analytic space over a $p$-adic field, equipped with a suitable \'etale map to a unit polydisk. We provide a formalism of \emph{imperfect relative period rings} over $X$, which lie inside the corresponding perfect relative period rings constructed by Kedlaya--Liu. Then we establish a relative version of the Fontaine--Cherbonnier--Colmez equivalence between $p$-adic local systems on $X$ and \'etale $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over such imperfect relative period rings, generalizing previous works of Andreatta--Brinon and others. Using this equivalence, we construct $p$-adic differential equations attached to de Rham local systems, carrying both geometric and arithmetic differential operators. This generalizes the work of Berger to the relative geometric setting. Along the way, we study a relative Fontaine--Sen theory on the decompletion of $\Gamma$-modules over the relative $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-period rings.

papers.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
papers.abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.

papers.title: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $\mu_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(\mu_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $\mu_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$

papers.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
papers.abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

papers.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Plane Curves defined from Chebychev polynomials
papers.abstract: For any $d\geq 4$ we determine the automorphism groups of the algebraic curves \[ \mathcal{C}_d : y^d = \varphi_d(x), \] where $\varphi_d(x)$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $d$, defined over a field $k$ with $p:=\operatorname{char}(k) \nmid 2d$. For $d>4$, it is $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, except when $2d=p^r+1$ or $4d=p^r+1$ for some $r\geq 1$. In these cases it is, respectively, $(\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z})\rtimes S_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times S_3$. Two ingredients used here are a description of all total inflection points on $\cC_d$, and knowledge of the group of fractional linear transformations that preserve the set of zeros of $\varphi_d$.
